Payment is the last step of a checkout. Wrap the parts in Payment with the order total and an onPay callback, then place ExpressCheckout, PaymentMethods, BillingAddress, PayButton and PaymentStatus where they fit your layout. Payment owns the state between them, so the button label follows the chosen method: “Pay $123.45” for a card, “Continue to PayPal”, “Pay $30.87 today” for Pay in 4.

The card form detects the brand from the first digits and swaps its mark only when the brand changes. It groups digits as you type, 4-6-5 for American Express, writes the expiry as MM/YY with the slash added for you, and accepts “1/27”, “0127” and pasted numbers with spaces or dashes. Each field is checked on blur or once it’s complete, then live, so an error clears the moment it’s fixed. onPay gets a typed request with the card details or saved card, the amount, the billing choice and a fresh idempotency key. Return nothing or { status: "succeeded" } to finish: the button shows a check, holds for 700 ms and calls onComplete. Return { status: "declined", code } and the error appears above the methods with copy written for that code, focus moves to it, the card stays filled in and “Try another card” clears it. Return { status: "requires_action" } to open the “Confirm with your bank” dialog, where renderChallenge mounts your 3-D Secure step.
